chunks: Bukayr ibn Aʿyan narrated from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him saying: “If a man divorces his wife and brings two just witnesses during the beginning of her waiting period ('iddah), then he has no right to divorce her again after that until her waiting period ends or he takes her back.”

key_terms.تَنْقَضِيَ: to come to an end or expire
key_terms.شَاهِدَيْنِ: two witnesses required to testify to the divorce
key_terms.طَلَّقَ: divorced; the act of issuing divorce
key_terms.عَدْلَيْنِ: upright and just, describing the required witnesses
key_terms.يُرَاجِعَهَا: to take her back or reconcile with her within the revocable period

ai.seo_question: Can a man divorce his wife again during her same 'iddah after a witnessed divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning divorce and the waiting period ('iddah). It states that once a valid divorce has occurred with the testimony of two just witnesses, the husband cannot issue another divorce during the same waiting period unless he first reconciles with her or waits for the 'iddah to end.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4755 - Bukayr ibn Aʿyan narrated from Abu Jafar Imam Al-Baqir (as), who said:

"If a man divorces his wife and brings two just witnesses to bear witness to it during her waiting period ('iddah), he cannot divorce her again after that until her waiting period ends or he reconciles with her."
